headline: Anthropic endorses plan to pace AI development, backed by OpenAI and Google DeepMind
summary: Anthropic and OpenAI, along with over 1,100 employees from major AI labs, signed an open letter advocating for tools to deliberately slow AI development, not an immediate pause. This initiative is tied to Anthropic's own research on AI self-improvement.
details: Anthropic and OpenAI, alongside over 1,100 employees from major AI companies, endorsed the 'Pacing the Frontier' letter on July 28. The letter asks the US government to support international efforts to build technical and governance tools for a deliberate, verifiable AI slowdown. It explicitly does not call for an immediate pause.

This distinction is crucial: an immediate pause can be dismissed, but a call for infrastructure to pace development later is harder to ignore. The signatories are asking for the option to slow things down before it becomes necessary, making it a proactive rather than reactive request.

What sets this initiative apart is the rapid, company-level endorsement from both OpenAI and Anthropic, reported within hours of the letter's release. This swift backing elevates it beyond a typical employee petition, indicating significant internal alignment.

The letter garnered signatures from high-ranking individuals, including Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and co-founders, OpenAI's chief scientist Jakub Pachocki and Ilya Sutskever, Google DeepMind's head of AI safety Anca Dragan, and Meta's chief scientist Shengjia Zhao.

Anthropic's public statement directly linked its support to its June research, 'When AI Builds Itself,' which revealed Claude now writes over 80% of the code merged into Anthropic's production codebase. This ties the policy ask to concrete, measurable findings about AI's current capabilities.

headline_marked: AI hedge fund [[Situational Awareness sells public portfolio]] to Citadel, retains $5B Anthropic stake
headline: AI hedge fund Situational Awareness sells public portfolio to Citadel, retains $5B Anthropic stake
summary: Leopold Aschenbrenner's AI-focused hedge fund, once returning 439%, faced steep losses, leading to the sale of most public stocks to Citadel, but still holds a valuable private stake in Anthropic.
details: Situational Awareness, founded by former OpenAI researcher Leopold Aschenbrenner, has sold the majority of its public stock portfolio to Ken Griffin’s Citadel. This follows steep losses over the past month, as reported by The Wall Street Journal. The fund's overall assets fell to roughly $10 billion from around $20 billion.

Aschenbrenner, 25, launched the fund in 2024 with no prior trading experience. He gained prominence for his investment thesis on AI scaling requiring significant build-up in semiconductors, compute, memory, and energy infrastructure. He was previously dismissed from OpenAI over an improper disclosure of internal information.

The fund initially saw immense success, returning 439% for the year through June and growing assets under management to as much as $45 billion. However, positions dropped sharply amid a broader decline in AI infrastructure investments. Losses were amplified by leverage.

Hardest-hit stocks included memory chip producers SK Hynix and Sandisk, clean energy developer Bloom Energy, and neocloud provider Nebius Group, all plummeting over 30%. Public investors grew concerned that massive capital expenditures weren't translating into near-term revenue.

Despite losses, Aschenbrenner invited clients to commit fresh capital, but the appeal didn't garner the hoped-for commitments. Citadel's purchase fits its pattern of acquiring attractive assets from leveraged players.
Crucially, Situational Awareness did not sell its private company investments, most notably its stake in Anthropic. This stake is currently valued at $5 billion and is seen as an appreciating asset.

Anthropic was last valued at $965 billion in May and is expected to go public as soon as October, potentially at an even higher valuation. A windfall from these shares could potentially offset some of the public-market losses.
Other private investments include chipmaker MatX and AI data center startup Fluidstack, which was reportedly in talks to raise a new round at an $18 billion valuation.
